outcome: Help patients find the right approved service and appointment faster; benefits include lower abandonment, reduced call volume, better utilisation, and documented escalation.
overview: Patients abandon booking journeys because service directories, eligibility rules and schedules live in disconnected systems across web, app and contact centre. This solution provides an AI-assisted patient-access front door that understands a stated need in Arabic or English, matches it to approved services with reasons, checks eligibility, and books or reschedules directly against live EHR and scheduling systems — escalating safely to a human whenever symptoms fall outside permitted routing. Preparation guidance and reminders follow automatically, and every escalation is documented. An 8–12-week pilot against an agreed baseline targets shorter booking journeys, better slot utilisation, fewer avoidable no-shows and lower contact-centre pressure.

benefits.text: Cut selected patient booking-journey time by a target 30%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate against the customer’s own journey baseline during the pilot — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Reduce avoidable no-shows and unused slots through eligibility-checked booking and automated preparation guidance
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Improvement depends on schedule-data freshness and reminder-channel reach; measured against a pre-pilot no-show baseline

benefits.text: Deflect routine scheduling contacts from the contact centre while recording 100% of clinical or urgent escalations
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Containment level depends on directory completeness and the escalation rules the customer approves; escalation logging is a design property verified in UAT

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); patient-identifiable data stays in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, in line with UAE and Saudi health-data regulations

notFor.situation: No machine-readable service directory or scheduling API into the EHR/PAS
notFor.why: The solution books against live schedules; without APIs it can only hand off to a call, which removes most of the value

notFor.situation: Expectation of autonomous clinical triage without human escalation
notFor.why: The solution routes symptoms outside approved rules to clinicians by design; it does not make triage decisions, and local health-authority requirements (DHA/DoH/SFDA/MOH) apply to anything that would

notFor.situation: Single-site clinic with low contact volume
notFor.why: Integration and governance cost is unlikely to be recovered from a small booking volume

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns routing-rule approval and escalation policy · Duration: 8–12-week pilot; 16–24 weeks to production rollout
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, conversational-AI engineer, integration engineer; customer access owner, clinical escalation owner, EHR/PAS integration lead, privacy and security approvers · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Journey and routing-rule discovery
2) Directory, scheduling and EHR integration
3) Channel build and Arabic/English content calibration
4) Safety, privacy and accessibility testing
5) Controlled launch on selected services
6) Stabilisation, benefit review and handover
deliverables: Bookings reconcile 100% with the EHR/PAS schedule
Urgent and clinical escalations route correctly in drill scenarios and are fully logged
Arabic and English journeys pass accessibility review
Load and security tests passed at agreed volumes
Access agents and service owners complete operational UAT
languages: English delivery; Arabic and English patient-facing channels
